scan_metadata.paper: Diffusion differentiable resampling (Andersson & Zhao, ICML 2026; arXiv:2512.10401)
scan_metadata.explanation: Static scan of README, diffres/*.py, demos (4 scripts + notebook), tests (3), experiments (scripts, run_*.sh, summary). No code was executed. Five tools selected over three modules; six execution assignments proposed (two marked optional). Experiments other than one smallest-setting LGSSM and one GMS run are verification references only; CIFAR-10, Lotka-Volterra training, profiling, sweeps and summaries are omitted with reasons.

tutorials.title: Diffusion resampling example (Gaussian mixture)
tutorials.description: Official tutorial: builds a 5-component GM prior in d=10 with linear Gaussian likelihood (dy=2), importance-weights 1024 prior samples, resamples with diffusion_resampling(a=-2, ts=linspace(0,1,33), integrator=jentzen_and_kloeden, ode=True), ensemble_ot(eps=0.3) and multinomial, and plots against exact posterior samples (gm_lin_posterior + sampling_gm). Outputs: one saved figure (image/png); no printed numbers.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: The repository's only tutorial and the README-referenced demonstration of diffusion_resampling on a user-style weighted particle set. Owns diffres_resample_particles_diffusion. Self-contained (PRNGKey(666), no external data); n=1024, d=10 keeps (n,n,d) score arrays ~84 MB.

tutorials.title: Resampling unit tests
tutorials.description: Weighted 1-D sample (n=10000, uniform on [-2,2], log weights = N(0; x, 1)); checks sliced-Wasserstein distance between resampled and weighted original for soft_resampling(alpha=1-1e-3), gumbel_softmax(tau=1e-3) [atol 1e-4], diffusion_resampling(a=-0.5, ts=linspace(0,1,16)) for integrators euler/lord_and_rougemont/jentzen_and_kloeden x ode/sde, diffrax (ode only), tweedie (sde only) [atol 1e-3], ensemble_ot(eps=0.1) [atol 3e-3]; test_diffres_versions checks diffusion_resampling == diffusion_resampling_generic with the empirical Gaussian reference (exact allclose).
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Most complete runnable verification of every resampler option. Owns diffres_resample_particles_baseline; also the main numeric check for the diffusion tool. Risk: n=10000 is hard-coded at module level; diffusion/OT/Gumbel materialise (n,n) float64 arrays (~0.8 GB each), likely above the heavy.sh limit while MemAvailable is ~3.4 GB. If the unmodified test is killed, a recorded driver re-running the same test bodies at smaller n is needed (tolerances were calibrated at n=10000).

tutorials.title: Filter and SMC unit tests
tutorials.description: 1-D OU-type LGSSM (semigroup exp(-dt), trans_cov 1-exp(-2dt), H=1, R=1, m0=0, P0=1, 101 observations ys=N(0,1) draws). test_kf: kf+rts match closed-form GP regression mean/variance/nll. test_smc: smc_feynman_kac with multinomial, multinomial_stopped, stratified, systematic (1000 particles) nll vs KF nll rtol 6e-2. test_diffres: diffusion_resampling inside SMC (a=-0.5, ts=linspace(0,2,8), sde, 4 integrators) rtol 5e-2. test_ensemble_ot: eps=0.1, rtol 7e-2.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Direct verification of the particle-filter tool on an LGSSM with every resampler and of the exact Kalman reference (test_kf also supports module gaussian_filters). Owns diffres_run_lgssm_particle_filter. Cheap (1000 particles, d=1).

tutorials.title: Gradient of PF log-likelihood: diffusion vs stopped-gradient multinomial
tutorials.description: Simulates a 1-D LGSSM with simulate_lgssm (F=0.5, Q=1, H=1, R=1, P0=1, PRNGKey(666), default 128 steps); computes the exact KF negative log-likelihood and its gradient w.r.t. theta=(scale of F, scale of H) at theta=(0.2,0.2), then 1000 Monte Carlo jax.value_and_grad evaluations of the PF nll with diffusion_resampling (a=-1, T=2, 128 steps, euler, ode, jitter=1e-5) and multinomial_stopped (8 particles); prints KF loss/grad, MC means and gradient RMSEs.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Traceable deterministic reference for simulate_lgssm and the Kalman nll/gradient (owns diffres_run_lgssm_kalman_filter and diffres_simulate_lgssm_data, module gaussian_filters) and supporting evidence for the particle-filter tool's gradient option. Bounded with upstream defaults (--nsteps 128 --nparticles 8; 1000-iteration loop is hard-coded but each call is tiny).

tutorials.title: LGSSM experiment, diffusion resampling
tutorials.description: Per MC seed: simulate LGSSM (F=0.5, Q=1, H=1, R=0.5), PF-vs-KF loss over a hard-coded 128x128 parameter grid, filtering KL and Bures errors between PF weighted moments and KF moments at the true parameters (lines 115-122), and L-BFGS-B (jaxopt) parameter estimation. Saves ./lgssm/results/*.npz relative to cwd.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Only upstream source of the PF-vs-KF filtering error metrics (tools.kl, tools.bures on PF moments) used by the particle-filter tool's optional compare_to_kalman output. Run once at the smallest upstream-supported settings (e.g. --id_l=0 --id_u=0 --nsteps=32 --nparticles=16 --a=-1. --T=1. --dsteps=4 --integrator=euler) from a scratch cwd containing a copy of rnd_keys.npy and a lgssm/results directory. Needs jaxopt, which pyproject.toml does not declare. Full 100-seed sweep (run_lgssm.sh) is out of scope.

tutorials.title: Gaussian-mixture experiment, diffusion resampling
tutorials.description: Same model as the notebook but with a quantitative metric: sliced Wasserstein (p=1) between exact posterior samples and diffusion-resampled samples, plus the posterior-mean residual. Defaults dx=8, dy=1, c=5, nsamples=10000. Saves ./gms/results/*.npz relative to cwd.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Optional quantitative supporting check for diffres_resample_particles_diffusion (the notebook has no printed metric). Smallest settings: --id_l=0 --id_u=0 --nsamples=1000 (upstream argument; default 10000 would need ~6 GB for (n,n,d) arrays) --a=-1. --T=1. --nsteps=8 --integrator=euler, run from a scratch cwd with rnd_keys.npy and gms/results.

tool_review.task: Resample a user-supplied weighted particle set with diffusion resampling (empirical diagonal Gaussian reference), returning equally weighted, differentiable-by-construction resamples.

implementation.symbol: diffusion_resampling(key, log_ws, samples, a, ts, integrator="euler", ode=True, jitter=0., einsum=False)

tool_review.inputs: samples (n, d) [or (n, ...)] as inline JSON list or path to .npy/.csv; log_weights (n,) or weights (n,); a < 0 (docstring: must be negative); T and nsteps -> ts=linspace(0,T,nsteps+1) as in every upstream caller (optionally explicit ts); integrator in {euler, lord_and_rougemont, jentzen_and_kloeden, diffrax (ode only), tweedie (sde only)}; ode bool; jitter >= 0; seed int -> jax.random.PRNGKey(seed). Enable jax_enable_x64 as all upstream callers do. Keep einsum internal (GPU-utilisation switch only).
tool_review.outputs: resampled particles (n, d) saved to file plus inline when small; output log weights (uniform -log n); brief summary (input ESS, weighted mean of input vs mean of output).
contract_notes: diffusion_resampling uses exp(log_ws) directly as normalised weights for the reference mean/variance; every upstream caller normalises with logsumexp first. Wrapper must normalise (and say so) or reject unnormalised input; do not silently change results otherwise.
Unsupported combinations raise NotImplementedError upstream (diffrax with ode=False, tweedie with ode=True, tme). Preserve that error meaning.
With integrator=diffrax every scan step re-solves the full ODE over [0,T] (upstream behaviour); cost is nsteps x a full solve.
Memory: the ensemble score materialises (n, n, prod(d)) float64 arrays per step (~8*n^2*d bytes each); a resource guard on n^2*d is advisable on this machine.

verification.compare: resamples from the tool with the notebook's inputs/key equal direct upstream diffusion_resampling output (allclose); qualitative match to the saved figure
sliced-Wasserstein distance to the weighted input <= 1e-3 for all 8 tested integrator/ode combos; equality with direct upstream call
printed SWD error vs exact posterior samples reproduced by the tool on the same inputs

tool_review.reason: Core contribution of the paper; README quick start is exactly this call.

tool_review.task: Resample the same kind of weighted particle set with one of the baseline resamplers implemented in the repository, for comparison with diffusion resampling.

implementation.symbol: multinomial, stratified, systematic, multinomial_stopped, ensemble_ot(eps=None->1/log n, implicit_diff=True), soft_resampling(alpha), gumbel_softmax(tau)

tool_review.inputs: samples, log_weights/weights, seed as above; method in {multinomial, stratified, systematic, multinomial_stopped, ensemble_ot, soft, gumbel_softmax}; method parameters eps (+implicit_diff) for ensemble_ot, alpha in [0,1] for soft, tau > 0 for gumbel_softmax.
tool_review.outputs: resampled particles (n, d) and output log weights (soft_resampling returns non-uniform normalised log weights; others uniform), same summary as the diffusion tool.
contract_notes: systematic/stratified and ensemble_ot assume normalised weights (cumsum compared to (i+u)/n; OT marginal b=exp(log_ws)).
ensemble_ot, gumbel_softmax also materialise (n, n) arrays.
multinomial_stopped differs from multinomial only in gradients; forward output is identical given the same key.

verification.compare: SWD to weighted input within atol 1e-4 (soft, gumbel) and 3e-3 (OT eps=0.1); equality with direct upstream calls
these four resamplers inside SMC reproduce KF nll within rtol 6e-2
ensemble_ot(eps=0.3) and multinomial outputs on notebook inputs

tool_review.reason: Coordinator guidance (a); all baselines are concrete public functions with tests. One tool with a method switch avoids seven near-identical wrappers.

tool_review.task: Run a bootstrap particle filter (SMC) on a linear Gaussian state-space model given as JSON matrices with a chosen resampler (diffusion or any baseline), returning filtering particles/weights, ESS and the log-likelihood estimate; optionally its gradient w.r.t. model matrices and a comparison with the exact Kalman filter.

implementation.symbol: smc_feynman_kac(key, m0, log_g0, m_log_g, pytree=ys, nparticles, nsteps=N, resampling, resampling_threshold=1., return_path=True)
implementation.model_construction: bootstrap m0_sampler/log_g0/m_log_g as in tests/test_filters.py lines 59-73 (and experiments/lgssm/diffusion.py lines 63-80), generalised from diagonal/1-D to full matrices using the Cholesky factors exactly as diffres.tools.simulate_lgssm does and diffres.tools.logpdf_mvn_chol for the observation potential; for diagonal inputs this reduces to the test code.

tool_review.inputs: F (dx,dx), Q (dx,dx), H (dy,dx), R (dy,dy), m0 (dx,), P0 (dx,dx), ys (N+1, dy) with ys[0] the time-0 observation (used by log_g0, matching kf); nparticles; resampler name + its parameters (same set as the two resampling tools); resampling_threshold in (0,1]; seed; return_gradient bool; compare_to_kalman bool.
tool_review.outputs: filtering particles (N+1, s, dx) and log weights (N+1, s) saved to .npz; weighted filtering means/covariances; ESS (N+1,); negative log-likelihood (upstream returns nll; also report log-likelihood = -nll); optional jax.value_and_grad gradient of nll w.r.t. F and H (as in demos/gradient_variance2.py and the L-BFGS objective in experiments/lgssm); optional KF nll and mean KL / Bures filtering errors.
contract_notes: Arbitrary Python model callables cannot be passed over MCP; only the LGSSM family is exposed. Nonlinear/non-Gaussian models are omitted (see tool_review).

Gradient semantics depend on the resampler: multinomial/stratified/systematic give gradients that ignore the resampling step; multinomial_stopped, diffusion, OT (use implicit_diff=False as the LGSSM experiments do), soft, gumbel are the differentiable options. Report this rather than altering it.
To reproduce tests bit-for-bit the wrapper must draw random numbers in the same order/shape as the test m0_sampler and m_log_g.

verification.compare: tool nll on the test model equals direct upstream smc_feynman_kac nll with the same key and is within rtol 6e-2/5e-2/7e-2 of the KF nll
MC mean of tool gradients (diffusion, multinomial_stopped) close to the KF gradient printed by the demo; single-key gradient equals direct upstream value_and_grad
KL/Bures filtering errors at the true parameters for seed 0 reproduced by compare_to_kalman

tool_review.reason: Coordinator guidance (b); the PF is the paper's main downstream use of differentiable resampling and an LGSSM given as matrices is a realistic MCP input with an exact reference.

tool_review.task: Exact Kalman filter (and optional RTS smoother) for the same LGSSM JSON specification: filtering/smoothing means and covariances, exact negative log-likelihood, optional gradient of the nll w.r.t. F and H; the reference against which particle filters are judged.

implementation.symbol: kf(ys, m0, v0, semigroup, trans_cov, obs_op, obs_cov) -> (mfs, vfs, nll, mps, vps); rts(mfs, vfs, mps, vps, semigroup) -> (mss, vss)

tool_review.inputs: F, Q, H, R, m0, P0, ys as in the particle-filter tool; smooth bool; return_gradient bool.
tool_review.outputs: filtering means (N+1,dx) and covariances (N+1,dx,dx); nll and log-likelihood; optional RTS smoothing means/covariances; optional gradient of nll w.r.t. F and H.
contract_notes: R + H P H^T must be positive definite (Cholesky in kf_update).
nll includes the time-0 observation update.

verification.compare: kf/rts on the test OU model equal closed-form GP regression mean, variance and nll (allclose)

loss_true and grad_true printed by the demo (KF nll and gradient at theta=(0.2,0.2) on simulated data) reproduced by the tool given theta-scaled F, H (chain rule: dtheta1 = sum(dF * I), dtheta2 = sum(dH * ones))

tool_review.reason: Coordinator guidance (b): exact reference on linear Gaussian SSMs; tested against a closed form.

tool_review.task: Simulate a latent trajectory and observations from an LGSSM JSON specification, so users can generate inputs for the two filter tools.

implementation.symbol: simulate_lgssm(key, semigroup, trans_cov, obs_op, obs_cov, m0, v0, nsteps) -> (xs (N+1,dx), ys (N+1,dy))

tool_review.inputs: F, Q, H, R, m0, P0 (Q, R, P0 positive definite), nsteps N, seed.
tool_review.outputs: xs (N+1, dx), ys (N+1, dy) saved to .npz/.json for reuse by the filter tools.
contract_notes: Grouped with module gaussian_filters (LGSSM utilities) although the callable lives in diffres/tools.py; no other diffres.tools function is exposed.

verification.compare: ys from the tool with key = split(PRNGKey(666))[0] equal the demo's simulated ys (exact), which then feed the KF reference values

tool_review.reason: Small but independently useful and makes the filter tools composable without user-side code; used by every LGSSM workflow upstream.

Requires Python callables ref_sampler, logpdf_trans, score_ref; the only concrete instantiation in the repo (tests/test_resampling.py::test_diffres_versions) reproduces diffusion_resampling exactly, so a JSON-exposable version would add no capability without inventing reference families.
Exposed only as the integrator option of diffres_resample_particles_diffusion; tests/test_integrators.py is supporting evidence.
Returned as an output of the particle-filter tool and resampling summaries.
Used only to score PF moments against KF as in experiments/lgssm; exposed via compare_to_kalman.

Peripheral to the paper (only builds the REINFORCE baseline in demos/gradient_variance.py), no test, and upstream draws xT with the unsplit key (key_last unused). Could be added later as a smoothing option of the PF tool with demos/gradient_variance.py as reference.
Benchmark references used by the notebook, gms experiments and integrator tests; they generate held-out truth rather than serve a user task on the user's particles.

tool_review.candidate: Particle filter for nonlinear / non-Gaussian SSMs (e.g. Lotka-Volterra Poisson model)
tool_review.reason: smc_feynman_kac needs Python callables for the proposal and potential; the only non-Gaussian model (experiments/lokta) is hard-coded and tied to NN training. Accepting user code or expression strings would be new functionality.

tool_review.candidate: Parameter estimation by L-BFGS-B on the PF loss
